reading: auroc_txtemb_to_Y should sit at CHANCE (~0.5) -- a text-only detector with NO model internals should not be able to predict Y from the composed prompt's own surface text, since the bridge entity is never written there. Above chance would mean the benchmark leaks the answer into the prompt, the artifact Hussain & Kantarcioglu's own audit found inflating much of this literature. A LARGE frac_zero_overlap (most items have NO surface overlap at all between prompt and target) combined with a far-from-0.5 AUROC driven by the small nonzero-overlap minority is a DIFFERENT, narrower finding than a benchmark-wide leak -- report which case this is, do not present a skewed AUROC as evidence of a leak (or its absence) without checking frac_zero_overlap first.
